newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil slips five cents.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil slips five cents.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps edged lower late on Wednesday as players tread cautiously amid uncertainties over whether or not a local trader would withdraw his buying support, brokers said on Wednesday.
April gas oil dipped five cents from this morning's levels to be quoted at $26.50/$26.70 per barrel.
Brokers said some players were apprehensive whether the local trader who had soaked up over three million barrels of gas oil recently could sustain his buying spree.
"There are some uncertainties and players are holding back," a broker said.
Jet/gas oil regrade remained quoted at a discount with offers edging lower to parity to meet bids which were at minus 20-cents.
Traders said jet fuel continued to be depressed on poor demand from Indonesia.
In the fuel oil market, the April/May spread was at a 25-cent backwardation. April was quoted at $97.50/$98.50 and May at $97.25/$98.25.
Traders said levels might move higher on perceived healthy demand from a local trader. They said India's April tender may also help boost sentiment.
India has issued a tender to buy 30,000 tonnes of high sulphur fuel oil for delivery April 19-23. The tender will close April 23 and is valid for one day.
South Korea's KEDO's tender to buy up to 64,000 tonnes of residual fuel will also help support prices, traders said.
